He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]], and briefly played for the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). ==High school career== Hernandez attended [[Miami Norland Senior High School|Miami Norland High School]] in [[Miami, Florida]], playing on three state championship teams. As a senior, he averaged 19.2 points and 9.1 rebounds per game and was the Miami Herald 8A-6A Player of the Year. In January 2016, Hernandez was named a McDonald's All American, and competed in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite news|last1=Kaufman|first1=Michelle|title=Cops say top UM basketball recruit assaulted man hiding with ex-girlfriend|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article101773392.html#1|access-date=December 5, 2017|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=September 14, 2016}} In the Under Armour Association circuit, he participated with Team Breakdown and averaged 16.1 points and 8.6 rebounds per game. He committed to Miami after considering offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] and [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite magazine|last1=Johnson|first1=Chris|title=Miami gets another elite recruit in five-star big man Dewan Huell|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/11/18/dewan-huell-commits-miami-hurricanes-bruce-brown|access-date=December 5, 2017|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=November 18, 2015}} He was rated as a five-star recruit and was ranked 28th in the 2016 high school class by [[ESPN]]. ==College career== As a freshman, he averaged 5.8 points and 3.1 rebounds per game. He showed marked improvement as a sophomore and scored a career-high 23 points in a victory over [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] on November 29, 2017.{{cite news|last1=Kaufman|first1=Michelle|title=Sophomore has career night as Hurricanes stay unbeaten with close win on the road|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article187330413.html|access-date=December 5, 2017|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=November 30, 2017}} Hernandez averaged 11.4 points and 6.6 rebounds per game as a sophomore while shooting 57 percent from the field. Following the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent and ultimately withdrew and returned to Miami.{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Dewan Huell returning to Miami for junior season |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/05/26/dewan-huell-returning-to-miami-for-junior-season/ |access-date=May 30, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=May 26, 2018}} In October 2018, he announced he had legally changed his name to Dewan Hernandez in honor of his mother, Christina Hernandez.{{cite news |title=Hurricanes forward Dewan Huell changes name to Hernandez |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/10/10/hurricanes-forward-dewan-huell-changes-name-to-hernandez/ |access-date=October 12, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=October 10, 2018}} Hernandez ultimately would not play for Miami in his junior season due to eligibility concerns relating to the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]] revolving around Christian Dawkins.{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25683869/miami-hurricanes-weigh-options-ncaa-rejects-dewan-hernandez-appeal-eligibility|title=Canes weigh options after Dewan Hernandez's appeal denied|date=January 4, 2019|first1=Mark|last1=Schlabach|first2=Jeff|last2=Borzello|work=[[ESPN]]}} After failing to qualify for eligibility twice,{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25762606/dewan-hernandez-miami-hurricanes-hopes-play-ncaa-committee-upholds-previous-rulings|title=Miami's Dewan Hernandez still hopes to play after ruling again upheld|date=January 14, 2019|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|work=[[ESPN]]}} Hernandez declared his entry for the [[2019 NBA draft]] on January 28, 2019.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/2019/01/28/ncaa-suspends-miami-dewan-hernandez-rest-season-christian-dawkins|title=Dewan Hernandez Decides to Leave Miami After Being Ruled Ineligible for Rest of Season|first=Alaa|last=Abdeldaiemjan|date=January 28, 2019|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} ==Professional career== === Toronto Raptors (2019–2020) === On June 20, 2019, Hernandez was drafted in the second round, 59th overall, in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/raptors-nba-draft-dewan-hernandez-1.5185012|title=Raptors happy to grab Dewan Hernandez with 2nd-last pick of NBA draft|date=June 21, 2019|first=David|last=Alter|work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]]}} On July 13, 2019, Hernandez was officially signed by the [[Toronto Raptors]] to an entry-level contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-sign-second-round-pick-dewan-hernandez-multi-year-contract/|title=Raptors sign second-round pick Dewan Hernandez to multi-year contract|date=July 13, 2019|work=[[Sportsnet]]}} On November 4, 2019, Hernandez received his first [[NBA G League]] assignment to the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-assign-2019-draft-pick-dewan-hernandez-905/|title=Raptors assign 2019 draft pick Dewan Hernandez to 905|date=November 7, 2019|first=Pete|last=Borkowski|work=[[Sportsnet]]}} In his first NBA G league game, Hernandez recorded 24 points, 10 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 blocks in a 94–109 loss to the Grand Rapids Drive.{{cite web|url=https://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2019/11/09/raptors-905-dewan-hernandez/|title=Dewan Hernandez Shines in Raptors 905 Debut Despite Loss|first=Lukas|last=Weese|date=November 9, 2019|work=Raptors Republic}} On August 12, 2020, Hernandez scored an NBA-career high 6 points and 2 assists, including clutch shots to help the Raptors win their sixth game in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA Restart Season]] against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] 125–121.{{Cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Daniel|date=August 12, 2020|title=Raptors bench unit powers late comeback over Sixers, 125-121|url=https://www.raptorshq.com/2020/8/12/21365743/nba-restart-recap-toronto-raptors-philadelphia-76ers-sixers-final-score|access-date=August 13, 2020|website=Raptors HQ|language=en}} On November 26, 2020, Hernandez was waived by the Raptors.{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2020/11/26/toronto-raptors-place-seldom-used-centre-dewan-hernandez-on-waivers.html|title=Toronto Raptors place seldom-used centre Dewan Hernandez on waivers|date=November 26, 2020|work=[[Toronto Star]]}} On December 19, he was signed and immediately waived by the Raptors for the purpose of joining their G-League team, [[Raptors 905]], as an affiliate player.{{cite web|url=https://www.raptorshq.com/2020/12/20/22191448/raptors-905-report-add-affliliate-players-dewan-hernandez|title=Raptors 905 look to add affiliate players, including Dewan Hernandez|date=December 20, 2020|first=JD|last=Quirante|work=Raptors HQ}} ===Raptors 905 (2021)=== On January 27, 2021, Hernandez was listed one of many players listed on the [[Raptors 905]] announced roster.{{cite web |title=RAPTORS 905 ANNOUNCE ROSTER AND SEASON SCHEDULE |url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-announce-roster-and-season-schedule/ |website=GLeague.NBA.com |access-date=January 29, 2021 |date=January 27, 2021}} ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2021)=== On February 26, 2021, Hernandez was traded to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] in exchange for guard [[Jarron Cumberland]].{{cite tweet|number=1365307966535184389|user=Raptors905|title=Raptors 905 have acquired guard Jarron Cumberland from the Rio Grande Valley Vipers, in exchange for forward Dewan… |date=February 26, 2021}} ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2021)=== On September 19, 2021, Hernandez signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web |title=Dewan Hernandez is joining Hapoel Tel Aviv |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/705247/Dewan-Hernandez-is-joining-Hapoel-Tel-Aviv |website=Eurobasket |access-date=September 19, 2021 |date=September 19, 2021}} In seven games, he averaged 7.3 points and 4.3 rebounds per game. Hernandez left the team on December 8, 2021.{{cite news |title=Dewan Hernandez leaves Hapoel Tel Aviv |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dewan-hernandez-leaves-hapoel-tel-aviv/ |website=Sportando |access-date=December 8, 2021 |date=December 8, 2021 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===Westchester Knicks (2022)=== On January 1, 2022, Hernandez was acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]] via returning player rights.{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 1, 2022}} ===Vaqueros de Bayamón (2022)=== On April 11, 2022, Hernandez signed with the [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of the BSN.{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|number=1513665847180636168|title=#BSN OFICIAL: El pívot Dewan Hernández es el nuevo refuerzo de los Vaqueros de Bayamón para la temporada 2022 del BSN. Hernández culminó con promedios de 20 PPJ y 9.1 RPJ este año en la G-League con Westchester Knicks. El jugador entra en sustitución de Devin Williams.|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=April 11, 2022|access-date=April 11, 2022}} ===Promitheas Patras (2024–2025)=== On October 7, 2024, Hernandez returned to active status by signing with Greek club [[Promitheas Patras B.C.|Promitheas]]. ===Mets de Guaynabo (2025)=== On April 23, 2025, Hernandez signed with the [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{Cite web|title=Former NBA players DeMarcus Cousins, Bryn Forbes and Dewan Hernandez signed with Puerto Rican team Mets de Guaynabo for the remainder of the 2025 season|url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/rumors/2025/04/23/former-nba-players-demarcus-cousins-bryn-forbes-and/84560333007/|access-date=January 30,
